products.challenge: BIO4 is listed as a current Stryker bone grafting product on stryker.com (2026-10-22), which supports the Stryker-Osiris arrangement continuing; the contract itself was not seen.
products.catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

products.name: map3 Cellular Allogeneic Bone Graft
products.ownership_history: Launched by RTI Surgical in 2014 using multipotent adult progenitor cell (MAPC) technology licensed from Athersys. FDA issued RTI a Warning Letter on 2017-11-08 (OBPO-1 18-01) holding that map3 could not be regulated solely as a 361 HCT/P. RTI ceased manufacturing and distributing map3 and incinerated its remaining inventory on 2018-12-19 under FDA observation; FDA's closeout letter is dated 2019-04-12 (MARCS-CMS 525318). RTI's spine business became Surgalign in 2020 (Surgalign went bankrupt in 2023; Xtant bought its assets), and RTI Surgical's OEM business was sold to Montagu Private Equity (announced 2020). Neither Xtant's FY2025 10-K nor RTI's current site lists map3: the product has been off the market since 2018.
products.composition: Cortical cancellous allograft chips, demineralized bone and cryopreserved multipotent adult progenitor cells (MAPC)

regulatory.reference: Section 361 HCT/P as claimed by RTI; FDA Warning Letter 2017-11-08 disputed this (map3 also subject to drug and biological product requirements); closeout letter 2019-04-12 after RTI stopped manufacture and distribution
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (361 homologous use)

applications.evidence_summary: One retrospective ALIF series (n=41) reported fusion equivalent to rhBMP-2 at 1 year (cited in the 2021 CBM systematic review); RTI's 30-patient ALIF/LLIF cohort (NCT02628210) completed 2020.
applications.caveats: Product may no longer be sold; a 2014 foot/ankle study was terminated after one patient.

evidence.title: Interbody spacers with map3 cellular allogeneic bone graft in ALIF or LLIF
evidence.finding: Completed June 2020; no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Illustrates the OEM-tissue-bank problem: when the distributor (Surgalign) failed, the brand effectively disappeared even though the processor (RTI) survived.

products.challenge: Discontinued 2018 (not merely absent from Xtant's list): FDA closeout letter 2019-04-12.

products.name: OsteoVive Plus viable bone allograft
products.ownership_history: Xtant Medical (Belgrade, MT; formerly Bacterin); Xtant acquired Surgalign's biologics assets (2023) and the nanOss production line from RTI, and sells OsteoSponge, OsteoSelect DBM, 3Demin fibers and OsteoVive Plus.
products.composition: Viable cell-containing cancellous bone with demineralized bone (Xtant describes OsteoVive Plus as a viable bone allograft)

regulatory.reference: No 510(k) for OsteoVive in openFDA (device_name OSTEOVIVE: no matches). Xtant FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-03-31) describes OsteoVive Plus as a viable bone allograft introduced in 2024 and carries a disease-transmission risk factor for it; 361 HCT/P status is inferred from the 10-K's statement that Xtant's products are HCT/Ps, 510(k)-cleared, or both
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (361 homologous use)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical study retrieved.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs; Xtant holds biologics contracts with Vizient, Premier and HealthTrust.
bd.notes: Over 670 independent commissioned sales agents and stocking distributors (10-K FY2024); growing private-label/OEM business, including supplying SimpliGraft and SimpliMax under distributor brands. Representative of the small-cap tissue-based spine biologics tier.

products.name: OssiGraft Prime viable bone matrix
products.ownership_history: Ossium Health (Indianapolis/San Francisco), private; raised a $52 million Series C; core business is organ-donor-derived bone marrow for transplant. OssiGraft distribution agreements with Extremity Medical (US) and Enovis.
products.composition: Vertebral-body-derived viable bone matrix, about 80% cancellous, from organ donors averaging 35 years; first case was an ankle fusion (July 2024); won a 2024 Orthopedics This Week Spine Technology Award

regulatory.reference: OssiGraft IFU (OHC-IFU-0002 Rev 05, hosted by Enovis): OssiGraft is an HCT/P that meets the 21 CFR 1271.10 criteria for regulation solely under section 361; no 510(k)/PMA/De Novo found
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (361 homologous use, presumed)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical data; marketing rests on younger donor age and vertebral-body sourcing (a 2018 lab study found vertebral-body marrow MSCs at least as osteogenic as iliac crest MSCs, PMID 29795650, unrelated to Ossium).
applications.caveats: Company claims only.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Distribution-partner model (Extremity Medical, Enovis); a new entrant competing on donor sourcing rather than clinical data.

products.name: Structural cortical allograft rings and blocks for ACDF (e.g., Cornerstone-SR, AVS/ Bio AVS, MTF and AlloSource cortical rings)
products.company: Multiple (MTF Biologics, AlloSource, LifeNet Health, RTI/Xtant; branded by Medtronic, Stryker, DePuy Synthes, Globus and others)
products.ownership_history: Commodity tissue-bank product supplied under private label to most spine companies; Medtronic's Cornerstone-SR ring was the carrier in its cervical rhBMP-2 trials.
products.composition: Machined cortical (fibula or femoral ring) or corticocancellous allograft spacers with a central window for graft; often paired with a filler (local bone, DBM, i-FACTOR, cellular allograft)

regulatory.reference: Section 361 HCT/P (minimally manipulated structural bone)
on_label_indications: Structural bone graft for cervical interbody fusion (homologous use); PEEK and titanium spacers are devices, not biologics

applications.evidence_summary: Meta-analysis of prospective plated ACDF studies: pseudarthrosis 4.8% with allograft vs 0.9% with autograft (Shriver 2015); 2024 meta-analysis of 34 studies/3,451 segments found structural allograft fusion rates not different from cages at 3-12 months but more hardware complications (Li 2024).
applications.caveats: Comparisons are across studies, not head-to-head RCTs; dysphagia rates do not differ between allograft and autograft (Shriver 2017).

evidence.title: Pseudoarthrosis rates in anterior cervical discectomy and fusion: a meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Overall pseudarthrosis 2.6%; autograft 0.9% vs allograft 4.8%.

evidence.title: Fusion rates at different times of cortical iliac crest autograft or allograft compared with cages after ACDF: a meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Structural allograft vs cage: no significant fusion difference at 3, 6 or 12 months; higher hardware complications with allograft.

bd.reimbursement: Inpatient bundled in MS-DRGs 471-473; physician add-on +20931 (structural allograft) is separately reportable and, unlike +20930, is not a Medicare 0-RVU bundled code (confirm current status indicator).
bd.notes: Low-margin commodity; the strategic value is in the filler sold with the ring (i-FACTOR, cellular allografts). MTF, AlloSource and LifeNet all private-label rings for device companies.

products.name: Cortoss Bone Augmentation Material
products.ownership_history: Orthovita developed Cortoss (CE mark 2001; FDA 510(k) clearance June 2009 after an IDE RCT); Stryker completed its acquisition of Orthovita on 2011-06-28.
products.composition: Injectable bis-GMA/bis-EMA resin composite reinforced with bioactive glass-ceramic particles (about 70% by weight); self-setting, nonresorbable, lower exotherm and stiffness closer to cortical bone than PMMA. PMMA itself is not a biologic.

regulatory.reference: K080108 (Cortoss Bone Augmentation Material; Orthovita; decision 2009-06-05; product code NDN, vertebroplasty cement). FDA recall Z-2101-2021 (Class 2, 10 cc cartridge, temperature excursion, terminated 2022-04-15) cites K080108 and shows US distribution in 2021.
on_label_indications: Augmentation of vertebral compression fractures via vertebroplasty (verify current Stryker IFU wording, including screw augmentation)

applications.evidence_summary: FDA-IDE RCT (Bae 2012, n=256, 2:1 vs PMMA, 21 US sites): noninferior; better pain at 3 months and function at 24 months; serious device-related AEs 4.3% in both arms; subsequent fractures 27.8% vs 31.9% (Gilula 2012).
applications.caveats: Orthovita-funded; modest clinical differences; Cortoss is bioactive but nonresorbable, so it is a 'biologic' only in the sense of surface bioactivity.

evidence.title: A prospective randomized FDA-IDE trial comparing Cortoss with PMMA for vertebroplasty: 24-month follow-up
evidence.finding: Noninferiority met; pain relief at 3 months and function at 24 months favored Cortoss; serious device-related AEs 4.3% each arm.

evidence.title: Subsequent fractures post-vertebral augmentation: analysis of a prospective randomized trial
evidence.finding: New fractures 27.8% Cortoss vs 31.9% PMMA; adjacent fractures 10.3% vs 18.2% in first-fracture subgroup.

bd.reimbursement: Inpatient VCF augmentation bundled in MS-DRGs 518-520 (back and neck procedures except spinal fusion); outpatient kyphoplasty/vertebroplasty paid under APCs with the material packaged; no separate HCPCS for the fill material.
bd.notes: Stryker Interventional Spine; niche vs Stryker's own PMMA products.

products.challenge: Cortoss has no dedicated stryker.com product page as of 2026-10-22 and appears only in VCF brochures; treat current US availability as unconfirmed. K number and IFU still not retrieved.
products.catalog_status_2026: Not on Stryker's bone grafting catalog page; a stryker.com site search for 'Cortoss' (2026-10-22) returns only a 'VCF Solutions Brochure', a '2019 IVS Portfolio Notebook', a VCF competitive comparison guide and an orthobiologics patents page, with no product page (the guessed /spine/products/cortoss.html URL is a 404).

products.name: KyphOs FS calcium phosphate bone cement (and other resorbable CPCs for vertebral augmentation)
products.ownership_history: Kyphon developed KyphOs FS for use with its balloon kyphoplasty system; Medtronic acquired Kyphon in 2007.
products.composition: Injectable, self-setting magnesium-substituted calcium phosphate cement that converts to a resorbable apatite; fast-setting 'FS' formulation for use after balloon tamp cavity creation

regulatory.reference: No 510(k)/PMA record under 'KyphOs FS' in openFDA (device_name KYPHOS: no matches; Kyphon/Medtronic Kyphon bone-cement 510(k)s are PMMA cements and tamps: K041584, K163032, K171938, K180700, K191148). Australia's TGA lists the Medtronic KyphOs FS calcium phosphate substitute (model C02B) as cancelled.
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; use with balloon kyphoplasty to fill the cavity in vertebral compression fractures (verify current labeling)

applications.evidence_summary: RCT of CPC vs PMMA in balloon kyphoplasty (Blattert 2009, n=56 patients/60 fractures): equivalent pain relief, but 9 radiographic losses of correction from cement failure in the CPC arm (burst-type fractures) vs none with PMMA; authors did not recommend routine CPC kyphoplasty. Small Korean series showed better Cobb correction but weaker support with CaP.
applications.caveats: The Blattert RCT tested a CPC (brand not stated in abstract); the mechanical weakness of resorbable cements in burst morphology is the class-level caution. PMMA is not a biologic and remains the standard.

evidence.title: Suitability of a calcium phosphate cement in osteoporotic vertebral body fracture augmentation: RCT of balloon kyphoplasty, CaP vs PMMA
evidence.finding: Pain relief similar; 9/30 CaP vertebrae lost correction (cement failure in burst fractures) vs 0/30 PMMA; 2 PMMA embolisms.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into kyphoplasty payment (inpatient MS-DRG or outpatient APC); no separate payment for the cement.
bd.notes: Medtronic Interventional Spine; CPC is a small share of augmentation volume, which is dominated by PMMA kyphoplasty (57,646 Medicare kyphoplasties in 2015).

products.challenge: Could not confirm any US clearance or current availability. Tried openFDA name and applicant searches (Kyphon, Medtronic, 'calcium phosphate'), Medtronic news (2010 US launch was of KYPHON ActivOs 10 hydroxyapatite-PMMA cement, not KyphOs FS) and web search; the only hard record is the TGA cancellation. Treat as ex-US/unverified until Medtronic confirms.

products.name: LDGraft (low-dose encapsulated rhBMP-2)
products.ownership_history: Locate Bio Ltd (Nottingham, UK), private; raised GBP 9.2 million in April 2024 to fund the RESTORE study; US subsidiary Locate Bio Pty/Inc.
products.composition: rhBMP-2 pre-encapsulated in a resorbable polymer (dose-shielding microparticles) within a bone graft substitute carrier, designed for sustained 28-day release at doses well below Infuse

regulatory.reference: Breakthrough Device designation May 2023 (single-level ALIF, L3-S1, DDD); FDA IDE approval announced 2025-09-08. ClinicalTrials.gov has two LDGraft records: NCT06462729 (Locate Bio Pty Ltd; Phase 1/2, ALIF, n=40 estimated; IDE-flagged unapproved device; recruiting since 2024-11-12; sites in Newcastle, Australia and Fort Wayne, Nashville and Pinehurst, US; last update 2026-08-26) and NCT07858643 (Locate Bio Ltd; 'AMBITION', n=25, sites in Tbilisi, Georgia; started 2026-04-08). NCT06462729 is the registration that matches the Australia-plus-US IDE study.

applications.evidence_summary: RESTORE (NCT06462729): first-in-human, randomized 3:3:2 dose-finding, single-blind, two LDGraft doses vs 100% allograft in single-level ALIF (L3-S1) with cage and plate; n=40; sites in Australia (Newcastle) and US (Fort Wayne, Pinehurst, Nashville); started November 2024, primary completion December 2027. Preclinical: 120-sheep study reported all three doses equivalent to ICBG at 6 months.
applications.caveats: No human efficacy data; the brief's description of a TLIF/PLF trial was wrong, the trial is ALIF only.

evidence.title: A randomized study of LDGraft in single-level ALIF (RESTORE)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary endpoints CT fusion, no secondary surgery, ODI 15-point improvement, neuro status and no device-related SAE at 12 and 24 months.

pipeline.expected_milestone: RESTORE primary completion December 2027; pivotal IDE would follow (company statements)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; would be bundled like Infuse if approved.
bd.notes: Positioned as 'Infuse efficacy at a fraction of the dose' to neutralize the YODA safety narrative; small company likely to need a commercial partner.

products.challenge: Two separate registrations exist; the Australia-plus-US IDE study is NCT06462729. The sponsor's 'RESTORE' name was not seen on either record.

products.name: NB1 (rhNELL-1 with DBM)
products.ownership_history: Bone Biologics Corp (NASDAQ: BBLG), Burlington, MA; exclusive worldwide license from UCLA for NELL-1 in spine fusion, trauma and osteoporosis; historically MTF Biologics was a major shareholder and the DBM carrier partner (not confirmed in sources fetched here).
products.composition: Recombinant human NEL-like molecule-1 (NELL-1) osteoinductive protein combined with demineralized bone matrix; proposed as a more bone-specific signal than BMP-2 with less ectopic bone and inflammation

regulatory.reference: No US IDE yet; pilot study design reviewed by FDA Division of Orthopedic Devices in a Pre-Submission; pilot run under Australian HREC approval

applications.evidence_summary: NCT03810573: multicenter randomized pilot in up to 30 adults with single-level DDD (L2-S1, up to Grade 1 listhesis) undergoing TLIF in Australia; first two patients treated June 2024; expanded to six Australian sites September 2026 with enrollment targeted to finish by end of 2026; primary endpoints fusion at 12 and 24 months and ODI change; 12-month data expected Q4 2027. Only preclinical efficacy data exist.
applications.caveats: Comparator not specified in public materials; company reports cash runway only through Q2 2027.

evidence.title: Multi-center, prospective, parallel group, randomized pilot study of NB1 bone graft device in DDD patients undergoing TLIF
evidence.finding: Recruiting (Australia); primary completion December 2026.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Pilot 12-month data Q4 2027, then US IDE pivotal and PMA (company statements, Sept 2026)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Micro-cap with a single asset; the 'hard healers' (smokers, diabetics, obese) positioning overlaps directly with PearlMatrix's high-risk subgroup claims.

products.name: Osteogrow (rhBMP6 in autologous blood coagulum) / Osteogrow-C
products.ownership_history: Genera Research Ltd (Zagreb, Croatia; Slobodan Vukicevic), EU FP7-funded OSTEOGROW project; a related rhBMP6 product (AGA111, Angitia Biopharmaceuticals) was tested in a US/China TLIF RCT, relationship to Genera unverified.
products.composition: Recombinant human BMP-6 delivered in an autologous blood coagulum carrier, mixed with cancellous allograft (Osteogrow-A) or synthetic calcium phosphate ceramics (Osteogrow-C)

regulatory.reference: EU clinical trials only: EudraCT 2017-000860-14 (Osteogrow-A, PLIF, 143 randomized in Austria, ended 13 Mar 2023, results posted 11 Feb 2026) and a TLIF trial; no US IDE/IND found

applications.evidence_summary: Osteogrow-A phase II (EudraCT 2017-000860-14): randomized, double-blind, n=143 at three Austrian centers (62 ICBG standard of care, 61 high-dose 2 mg rhBMP6, 20 low-dose 1 mg) in PLIF for L3-S1 DDD; 20-month composite 'overall clinical success' was very low in every arm, bilateral bridging was observed in only 4-6% of subjects in any arm, and the sponsor concluded the success definition was overly strict; fewer serious AEs with Osteogrow (31.1% HD vs 54.1% SoC); results posted February 2026. A separate 63-patient placebo-controlled rhBMP6 (AGA111) TLIF RCT was presented at AAOS 2025. Earlier Genera trials were in distal radius fracture and high tibial osteotomy.
applications.caveats: The posted PLIF fusion numbers are implausibly low for any arm and should be read from the EU register directly before being quoted; no peer-reviewed spine publication retrieved.

applications.evidence_summary: Preclinical only: rabbit and sheep posterolateral fusion with rhBMP6/ABC plus ceramics (PMID 38086987).
applications.caveats: No human PLF data.

evidence.title: Patient- and evaluator-blinded non-inferiority study of Osteogrow in adults undergoing PLIF for degenerative disc disease (Osteogrow-A)
evidence.finding: Non-inferiority claimed on a composite endpoint with very low success in all arms; fewer SAEs with rhBMP6; trial ended March 2023, results posted February 2026.

evidence.title: Calcium phosphate ceramics combined with rhBMP6 within autologous blood coagulum promote posterolateral lumbar fusion in sheep
evidence.finding: Osteogrow-C produced radiographic fusion with complete integration to transverse processes in sheep.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No US filing announced; next step unclear (company website undated)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Academic-origin program; the autologous-blood-carrier concept avoids collagen sponge and is pitched as lower-dose, lower-inflammation BMP.

products.challenge: EU CTR results page read directly on 2026-10-22. As posted: arms Standard of Care n=62 (55 mITT), HD Osteogrow n=61 (56 mITT), LD Osteogrow n=20 (19 mITT); primary 'overall clinical success' at 20 months 1.9% SoC vs 0.2% HD (LD none), difference -1.7 points, one-sided 95% lower limit -5.2 against a -10 margin, reported as non-inferior; radiographic fusion 3.8/5.6% at 6 months, 4.4/6.0% at 12 months, 6.2% SoC vs 4.2% HD at 20 months (difference -2, lower limit -9.5); serious TEAEs 54.1% SoC, 31.1% HD, 25.0% LD; 3 deaths in SoC. These success and fusion proportions are implausibly low for PLIF and almost certainly reflect a unit or data-entry error in the register posting (e.g. fractions mislabeled as percent); the extraction is verified but the numbers should not be quoted as fusion rates without the sponsor's publication.

products.name: Intradiscal / degenerative disc biologics (rexlemestrocel-L, IDCT, VIA Disc NP) - not fusion products
products.ownership_history: Mesoblast (ASX/NASDAQ: MESO), DiscGenics (private, Salt Lake City), VIVEX Biologics (private, Miami; VIA Disc NP is a 361 HCT/P nucleus pulposus allograft).
products.composition: Rexlemestrocel-L: allogeneic STRO-3+ mesenchymal precursor cells, 6 million cells with hyaluronic acid, single intradiscal injection. IDCT (rebonuputemcel): allogeneic discogenic progenitor cells in a viscous carrier. VIA Disc NP: processed allogeneic nucleus pulposus tissue reconstituted with saline.

regulatory.reference: Mesoblast: FDA IND, RMAT designation, BLA planned Q3 2027 after MSB-DR004 (NCT06325566). DiscGenics: Fast Track; phase 3 NCT07254806 started December 2025. VIVEX: VIA Disc NP marketed as a 361 HCT/P (not an approved therapy) while running an IND-stage RCT (NCT06778447).

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells with and without hyaluronic acid for chronic low back pain: randomized, double-blind, concurrent-controlled 36-month study (MSB-DR003)
evidence.finding: Primary composite responder endpoint at 12 and 24 months not met in all subjects; MPC+HA reduced LS-mean pain vs saline at 12 and 24 months, with larger effects in patients with CLBP under 68 months; no treatment-related SAEs.

evidence.title: Rexlemestrocel-L + HA vs saline in moderate to severe chronic low back pain (MSB-DR004)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; primary completion July 2027; company guides top-line mid-2027 and BLA Q3 2027.

evidence.title: IDCT (rebonuputemcel) vs sham in single-level mild-to-moderate lumbar disc degeneration (phase 3)
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 31 sites; primary completion November 2027; follows completed phase 1/2 NCT03347708 (n=60).

evidence.title: Nucleus pulposus allograft (VIA Disc NP) vs sham for lumbar discogenic pain
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 19 sites; primary completion October 2027; the earlier VIA Disc NP registry (NCT04652687) was terminated and a 500-patient registry 3.0 (NCT06345690) is active.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Mesoblast BLA Q3 2027 if MSB-DR004 succeeds; DiscGenics and VIVEX phase 3 readouts late 2027

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; VIA Disc NP is billed today as a 361 tissue product in office/ASC settings with no established coverage.
bd.notes: Included only as context: these are injectables aimed at avoiding fusion, not fusion biologics. The first MSB-DR003 phase 3 missed its primary endpoint, which is why Mesoblast is running a second phase 3; VIA Disc NP's commercialization under 361 while in an RCT is a regulatory grey zone FDA has scrutinized for other 'structural tissue' allografts.

products.name: LinQ SI Joint Stabilization System (and TRAQ)
products.composition: Machined structural cortical bone allograft ('almond-shaped' with a graft window), placed posteriorly into the decorticated mid-joint; TRAQ (2026) is a cortical-piercing allograft variant engaging sacral and iliac cortices at four points. Window may be packed with DBM at surgeon discretion (physician descriptions; not in the IFU text retrieved).

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: SECURE (NCT04423120; Calodney 2024, PMID 38524688): prospective single-arm, 16 US sites, 122 implanted, composite responder 73.5% at 12 months, one procedure-related SAE; no CT fusion endpoint. Bovinet 2025 (PMID 40832586): retrospective 6-site cohort n=258, NRS 7.6 to 1.6 at mean 1.75 years. Ampomah 2025 (PMID 40828365): n=260, AE 1.9% at 6 months. LINQT RCT vs conservative management (NCT07558278, n=200, started Jul 2026) is the first randomized trial of any posterior allograft.
applications.caveats: All clinical data are pain/function case series by interventional pain physicians with company involvement; no radiographic fusion rate; no comparison to lateral transfixing implants; three MAC LCDs (2025) non-cover procedures without a transfixation device.

evidence.title: SECURE: single-arm multicenter prospective study of LinQ
evidence.finding: 73.5% composite responders at 12 months; one procedure-related serious AE.

evidence.title: Safety, efficacy and durability of outcomes: results from SECURE
evidence.finding: VAS and ODI significantly improved at 12 months; responder rate stable 66-74% across visits.

evidence.title: Minimally invasive posterior SI joint fusion with a novel cortical allograft: real-world long-term outcomes, multisite US cohort
evidence.finding: Mean NRS reduction 6.0 points at 91 weeks; no serious AEs reported.

evidence.title: Retrospective evaluation of adverse events in posterior approach with bone allograft
evidence.finding: AE incidence 2.3% at 3 months and 1.9% at 6 months; no device-related events.

evidence.title: Multicenter retrospective analysis of a posterior sacroiliac fusion device (LinQ)
evidence.finding: NRS 6.98 to 3.06 at mean 612 days; no major AEs.

evidence.title: LINQT: open-label RCT of LinQ vs conventional medical management
evidence.finding: Enrolling; primary endpoint composite responder at 6 months, follow-up 24 months.

evidence.title: TRAQTION: post-market single-arm study of TRAQ
evidence.finding: Enrolling; 24-month follow-up.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: PainTEQ's clinician page states LinQ and TRAQ are HCT/Ps 'regulated solely under Section 361' and 'not FDA-cleared or FDA-approved medical devices'. PainTEQ drove the 0775T (2022) and 27278 (2024) code applications using SECURE interim data. Company ranked on Inc. 5000 (2024). Office-based-lab 27278 physician payment ($13,834 in 2026) is the economic engine for interventional pain practices.

products.ownership_history: PainTEQ (Tampa, FL) private; majority growth recapitalization co-led by Signet Healthcare Partners and Windham Capital Partners, Aug 2025.
products.challenge: Tissue bank that processes LinQ not disclosed in any public source retrieved; 'DBM packed in the window' comes from physician/trade descriptions, not the IFU.

products.name: iFuse INTRA V and iFuse INTRA X Allograft Implant Systems
products.composition: INTRA V (formerly INTRA): single triangular cortical allograft; INTRA X: two small cylindrical bone allografts; both 'implantable bone products manufactured from sterilized recovered cadaveric bone tissue', placed intra-articularly through a ~2 cm posterior incision.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical study retrieved; SI-BONE's product pages cite only finite-element analysis of SI joint motion and state the results are 'not necessarily indicative of human clinical results'. The FY2025 10-K attributes reduced INTRA X demand to the 2024-2025 MAC LCDs precluding coverage of CPT 27278.
applications.caveats: Launched 2024 as a defensive entry into the interventional-pain posterior segment; no SI-BONE-sponsored trial lists the allograft products (NCT07565545 is the titanium INTRA Ti). Manufactured and distributed as HCT/Ps by an undisclosed third-party tissue bank.

evidence.title: iFuse INTRA Ti (titanium posterior-inferior intra-articular cortical-piercing implant) safety and effectiveness
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting (start Sep 2026); titanium successor billed under 27279, not the allograft.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: 10-K: 'Our iFuse INTRA/INTRA X implants are derived from human bone tissue ... manufactured and distributed by a third-party as HCT/P products'; 10-K maps INTRA X to CPT 27278 ($441 facility / $13,834 OBL physician fee 2026) and the titanium products to 27279. SI-BONE sells direct (89 territory managers, 83 clinical specialists, 320 agents, FY2025).

products.challenge: Tissue bank not named; no clinical data; the 2024 launch year comes from the 10-K product chronology, not a dated release.

products.name: SiLO Posterior SI-Fusion System (allograft)
products.composition: Single dowel of human cortical bone with three circumferential ridges ('Dowel Anchorage Design') and dual vertical side channels that accept additional bone graft during insertion; posterior intra-articular, non-transfixing. SiLO TFX (K221047, Oct 2022; titanium cone plus ilium and sacrum screws, graft placed in the barrel) is the company's 510(k) transfixing hybrid and is a device, not a biologic.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical series for the SiLO allograft was retrieved; the company reported >2,500 SiLO procedures in the US (June 2025 release) and a cadaveric study of SiLO TFX. Aurora launched 'Aurora Biologics' in late 2025 to sell biologics with its implants.
applications.caveats: Company-reported volume only; SiLO TFX revenue grew 135% in 2024 and aggregate SI implant sales +8.4% in 2025 (press releases), implying the titanium hybrid, not the allograft, is the growth product after the 2025 LCDs.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Aurora Spine (TSXV: ASG / OTC: ASAPF), FY2025 revenue $18.4M (+4.6%); SI implants are one of three product lines. Distributor-based sales.

products.challenge: Tissue processor not disclosed; no clinical outcomes paper found for the allograft; SiLO vs SiLO TFX volumes not separated.

products.name: CornerLoc SI Joint Fusion grafts
products.composition: Two machined cortical bone allografts placed orthogonally into the prepared posterior joint through two small incisions, with a demineralized bone matrix sponge; non-transfixing. The company's TransLoc 3D (K232878, Oct 2023) is a 3D-printed titanium modular posterior implant plus lateral-oblique screws (hybrid) and is a device.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical series of the allograft retrieved; physician and hospital pages (UK HealthCare) describe the technique and a 12-month ossification timeline. CornerLoc's registered studies (NCT05916092 SPARTAN n=240; NCT06487936 registry) cover the titanium TransLoc 3D.
applications.caveats: Company founded 2017 (Tulsa, OK); evidence for the graft product is descriptive only; the hybrid TransLoc 3D exists because the posterior allograft alone is non-covered under the 2025 LCDs.

evidence.title: SPARTAN: post-market study of TransLoc 3D screw-only vs hybrid constructs
evidence.finding: Company reports 91.7% improved in pain and function at 6 months (interim, unpublished).

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Private; sells surgery-ready trays to pain practices and ASCs. The DBM sponge is unbranded in all sources.

products.challenge: Tissue bank and the DBM brand are not disclosed; launch year inferred from the 2017 founding and 2018-2019 physician adoption, not a dated release.

products.name: PsiF Posterior SI Fusion allograft
products.composition: Structural allograft bone implant placed through a postero-inferior intra-articular trajectory into a decorticated channel in the articular joint, secured mortise-and-tenon in subchondral bone (Lynch 2022). PsiF DNA (510(k) May 2025, launched Jan 2026) is a titanium double-helix transfixing implant placed ilium-to-sacrum that is packed with graft and leverages self-harvested autograft; PsiFGuard (SpineGuard, K-cleared Oct 2024) is the drilling-guidance device.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: Lynch 2022 (PMID 36420375): 57-patient multicenter registry, back pain 6.8 to 3.8 at 6 months. Kaye 2024 (PMID 39087970): LSU Shreveport single-center series of 72 posterior fusions (83% LinQ, remainder PsiF), VAS -3.6 cm, no procedure-related AEs, 54% with one-year follow-up. Latif 2023 (PMID 37511749) is a technique paper for PsiF DNA.
applications.caveats: Small registries with company-affiliated authors; PsiF results are pooled with LinQ in the only independent series; no fusion imaging endpoint.

evidence.title: Minimally invasive inferior intra-articular SI joint fusion with allograft bone
evidence.finding: Back pain 6.8 to 3.8 at 6 months; all outcomes p<0.001; no fusion endpoint.

evidence.title: Posterior sacroiliac fusion surgery: retrospective single-center study (LinQ and PsiF)
evidence.finding: VAS -3.6 cm from 9.5; 38.5% with >=50% improvement; zero procedure-related AEs; 26% withdrawal.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Omnia Medical (Morgantown, WV), private. The shift from the PsiF allograft to the 510(k) titanium PsiF DNA (transfixing, 27279-eligible) is the clearest example of a posterior vendor re-engineering around the 2025 LCDs.

products.challenge: Omnia's site does not describe the original PsiF implant's material; its allograft nature is taken from Kaye 2024 ('sacroiliac fusion allograft implants ... PsiF System from Omnia Medical') and Lynch 2022. Tissue bank and launch year not disclosed.

products.name: Vyrsa Pro cortical allograft (Vyrsa V1 titanium is the device)

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical publication retrieved for Vyrsa Pro. Nevro's post-market study NCT06909292 (n=180, completed May 2025) covers the titanium Nevro1 transfixing system.

evidence.title: Post-market multicenter study of the Nevro1 SI transfixing and fusion system
evidence.finding: Completed May 2025; results not posted; titanium transfixing device, not the allograft.
